description: Decide perfect-phylogeny feasibility for characters with at most three observed states using expanded-column 2-SAT and explicit missing-state handling.

complexity.primary_time: O(taxa_count*character_count + character_count^2) word operations; expanded-column incompatibility tests use fixed-width taxon bit masks and Kosaraju scans a dense bounded adjacency matrix
complexity.primary_space: O(character_count^2) bounded implication graph and SCC state

source.method_title: The Three-state Perfect Phylogeny Problem Reduces to 2-SAT
source.license: No source-code license asserted; clean-room mathematical algorithm

input.zero_characters: Valid; the empty 2-SAT instance is satisfiable for any allowed positive taxa count.

contract.expanded_columns: Each original character c contributes three binary columns (c,0),(c,1),(c,2), whose 1-set is the taxa set having that state.
contract.positive_clauses: For each original character, add (x0 OR x1), (x0 OR x2), and (x1 OR x2), requiring at least two expanded columns to be selected.
contract.incompatibility_clause: For expanded columns from distinct original characters, add (NOT xu OR NOT xv) exactly when all four binary taxon patterns 00,01,10,11 occur.
contract.missing_state_extension: For a character with exactly two observed states, add (NOT x_missing OR NOT x_missing), forcing both observed state columns to be selected. One-state characters are constant and impose no compatibility restriction.
contract.decision_algorithm: Build the implication graph for the 2-CNF formula and use Kosaraju strongly connected components; the formula is satisfiable iff no variable and its negation share an SCC.
contract.output: 1 iff the matrix has a perfect phylogeny with at most three observed states per character; otherwise 0. No tree witness is emitted.
contract.bound: At most 24 Boolean variables and a conservative 284 clauses, including up to one missing-state unit per character; the implication graph has at most 48 literal vertices and 568 arcs.
contract.distinction: The existing directed_perfect_phylogeny package handles binary characters. This profile uses the three-state expansion and 2-SAT reduction, extended to preserve binary splits when a character has only two observed states.

workspace.meaning: Fixed forward/reverse implication matrices for at most 48 literal vertices, SCC state, and bounded recursion frames.
